name: Quest Mechanics
content:
SOFT & HARD MOVES

Throughout the Quest, the rules will occasionally call for the GM to take SOFT MOVES and HARD MOVES. These are narrative prompts that facilitate significant storytelling moments and reinforce the notion that actions have consequences, introducing new challenges for the players to overcome.

By default, Soft and Hard Moves are limited to the Quest phase of gameplay, but the group may opt to make them available during the Premessa and Intermezzo phases as well. Note that, since the group collectively holds the power and duties of the GM during an Intermezzo, any Soft or Hard Moves that come up during that phase must be handled by the group collectively.

SOFT MOVES

When the GM takes a Soft Move, they introduce a danger or complication that the players then have a chance to react to:

  • A bridge creaks ominously as the party crosses it.

  • The tavern suddenly goes quiet as a group of armed figures enters.

  • A letter arrives with a seal the party recognizes.

HARD MOVES

When the GM takes a Hard Move, they dictate a danger or complication that has immediate, irrevocable consequences.

  • The alarm sounds and guards flood the corridor—the party's cover is blown.

  • A wall collapses, blocking the exit.

  • The noble you were supposed to protect is assassinated before your eyes.

BANE & BOON

The dice tell a story. They do so in the moment as rolls determine the outcomes of specific actions, but in Renaissance, they also tug at the threads of fate over time. This is represented by BANE & BOON.

As players roll dice throughout the course of the game, those rolls will occasionally produce two special results: Sol 🌞 and Morte 💀:

  • Each Sol 🌞 moves the party one notch toward BOON - a very good event.

  • Each Morte 💀 moves the party one notch toward BANE - a very bad event.

Track the party's BANE/BOON status on a notched scale. The number of notches between neutral (center) and BANE/BOON (either end) is equal to the number of player characters in the party. A party with three player characters would have a BANE/BOON scale like this:

BANE ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- || ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- BOON

The party starts in a neutral state at the beginning of each Quest, in the center of the scale. Only player characters' dice rolls effect BANE & BOON. Rolls made by allied NPCs do not count.

When the party reaches BANE, the GM takes a Hard Move: they introduce a danger or complication that has immediate, irrevocable consequences. The GM is encouraged not to hold back. A BANE should be very, very bad.

When the party reaches BOON, the players propose their own "Hard Move," though in this case it's a good thing that has immediate, irrevocable consequences. The GM has full discretion to accept or reject the players' proposal, but is encouraged to be generous. The players can also ask the GM to dictate the BOON. Either way, don't hold back - a BOON should be an exceptional moment of triumph or good fortune.

After reaching BANE or BOON, the party's position on the scale resets back to neutral and the Quest continues.

The party may reach BANE/BOON any number of times during a Quest. The party's position on the BANE/BOON scale at the end of a Quest has no effect, and they start back at neutral at the beginning of the next Quest. We do not track BANE/BOON outside of the Quest phase of the game.

The GM may track BANE/BOON themselves or delegate the duty to a player. Either way, the Quest's current position on the BANE/BOON scale is always public information.

COMPAGNIA

COMPAGNIA are points that represent the camaraderie among the party members during a Quest. Compagnia are a shared resource. The party starts each Quest with a total Compagnia equal to the number of party members.

During the Quest, any time a party member makes a skill check (see the Dice Rolls section), before the roll is made, any player may propose using Compagnia to enhance the roll.

All players must agree in order for Compagnia to be used. This is an above-the-table discussion, meaning it's the players - not the characters - discussing the significance of the moment.

Once the decision to use Compagnia has been made, take a moment to weave it into the narrative. What is it about this party in particular that motivates or enables the character who is making the Skill Check to push themself beyond their normal limits?

If any Compagnia remains at the end of the quest, it may be used to benefit the characters who completed the Quest, as outlined in the Rest & Recovery section. Otherwise, the Compagnia is forfeited.
